title: The Throne verse, whole
tomorrow: finals, Dadi, Hana. is this more than one soul can carry?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Opening: about Him, then to Him, and every line answered. The line: first words, last words. Now the verse Dadi says last thing at night.
screen: `FIRST WORDS, LAST WORDS.` → `THE VERSE BEFORE SLEEP.`

segments.voice: Somebody posts one line from a song, and the group chat splits in two: does she mean it literally, or is it a picture? Muslim scholars have had a gentle version of that argument, over one word in one verse. The verse is the one Dadi says over Amira every night now that they share a hallway. Amira and her cousin Hana, still barely speaking about the bangles, have ended up arguing about the word instead.
screen: `LITERAL, OR A PICTURE?` → `ONE WORD, ONE VERSE.` → `AMIRA AND HANA, ARGUING.`

segments.voice: Weigh it first, phrase by phrase, in Pickthall's words. "Allah! There is no God save Him, the Alive, the Eternal. Neither slumber nor sleep overtaketh Him." No nap, no blink, no off switch. All in the heavens and the earth is His; no one intercedes except by His leave; He knows what is before people and behind them. Then the line with the word: "His throne includeth the heavens and the earth." Pickthall's throne is the Arabic kursi, and the verse is named for it: Ayat al-Kursi. So what is the kursi? One reading, reported from Ibn Abbas and preferred by the commentator al-Tabari: the kursi is His knowledge, and His knowledge takes in the heavens and the earth. Nothing sits outside what He knows. The other reading, also handed down from early authorities: the kursi is real, a footstool distinct from the Throne, vast beyond picturing, affirmed as Allah describes it without asking how. Here, scale is the point; we can't imagine it, and we aren't asked to. Both readings meet in the verse's next words: "He is never weary of preserving them." That's the line to tell a friend tonight: the Throne verse doesn't end on power. It ends on the absence of tiredness.
screen: `NEITHER SLUMBER NOR SLEEP.` · `KURSI AS HIS KNOWLEDGE.` · `KURSI AS REAL, WITHOUT ASKING HOW.` · `NEVER WEARY OF PRESERVING THEM.` · then, large: `HE DOES NOT TIRE.`

segments.voice: Copy one phrase of the verse by hand, slowly, on paper: neither slumber nor sleep overtaketh Him. Then put the pen down and let your shoulders drop for the rest of the sit, the way tired people do when someone else is keeping watch.
screen: `COPY ONE PHRASE BY HAND.` · `SHOULDERS DOWN. SOMEONE IS AWAKE.`
